## HEADER

-   **Description**: This script is used to compare the datafiles produced for the ERAP 3.0 update to those used in the 2.0 update.
-   **Original Author**: Brendan Chen
-   **Date of Creation**: 10/05/2025

```{r dependencies}
## libraries
library(tidycensus)
library(sf)
library(readxl)
library(tidycensus)
library(tigris)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(skimr)
library(urbnthemes)
options(scipen = 9999)
options(tigris_use_cache = F)

```

```{r load in data}

## Loading in original 2.0 data, 2.0 rerun data, and 3.0 data

data_catalog_index_old <- read_csv(here("data", "comparison-data", "data_catalog_index_nonspatial.csv")) %>% 
  select(-num_eli_renters)

data_catalog_2021_acs <- read_csv(here("data", "comparison-data", "data_catalog_index_2.0_2025.csv")) %>% 
  rename(hh_chars_subindex_value = hh_chars_value,
         median_monthly_housing_cost = median_monthly_housing_coust)

data_catalog_2023_acs <- read_csv(here("data", "comparison-data", "data_catalog_index_2025.csv")) %>% 
  rename(hh_chars_subindex_value = hh_chars_value,
         median_monthly_housing_cost = median_monthly_housing_coust)

```

```{r}
## comparison of data across runs/computers/users

data_catalog_2021_a = data_catalog_2021_acs

  read_csv()

data_catalog_2022_b = here::here("data", "final-data", "data_catalog_index_outcome_year_2018_census_year_2022.csv") %>%
  read_csv()

data_catalog_2023_a = file.path("C:", "Users", "wcurrangroome", "Box", "ERAP Update 2025", "Data Comparison", "data_catalog_index_outcome_year_2018_census_year_2023.csv") %>%
  read_csv()

data_catalog_2023_b = here::here("data", "final-data", "data_catalog_index_outcome_year_2018_census_year_2023.csv") %>%
  read_csv()

test_same_year_data = function(version1, version2) {
  result = left_join(
      version1 %>% rename_with(.cols = -c(geoid, state_name, county_name), .fn = ~ str_c(.x, "version1")),
      version2 %>% rename_with(.cols = -c(geoid, state_name, county_name), .fn = ~ str_c(.x, "version2"))) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = matches("version1$|version2$")) %>%
    mutate(
      version = str_extract(name, "(version1$|version2$)"),
      name = str_remove(name, "(version1$|version2$)")) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = version,
      values_from = value) %>%
    filter(version1 != version2)
  
  if (nrow(result) != 0) warning("The datasets are not identical")
  
  return(result)
}

test_same_year_data(data_catalog_2023_a, data_catalog_2023_b)
test_same_year_data(data_catalog_2022_a, data_catalog_2022_b)
test_same_year_data(data_catalog_2021_a, data_catalog_2021_b)
```



```{r}

# Merge by geoid
acs_2021_merged <- merge(
  data_catalog_index_old,
  data_catalog_2021_acs,
  by = "geoid",
  suffixes = c("_old", "_new")
)

# Compare each common variable and create flag columns
# Find the columns (excluding ID) that exist in both data frames
common_cols <- intersect(
  setdiff(names(data_catalog_index_old), "geoid"),
  setdiff(names(data_catalog_2021_acs), "geoid")
)

# Create flags for columns that are different
for (col in common_cols) {
  old_col <- paste0(col, "_old")
  new_col <- paste0(col, "_new")
  flag_col <- paste0(col, "_flag")

  acs_2021_merged[[flag_col]] <- as.integer(
    acs_2021_merged[[old_col]] != acs_2021_merged[[new_col]]
  )
}

# total how many columns differ between the two dfs
acs_2021_merged$any_diff <- as.integer(rowSums(acs_2021_merged %>% select(ends_with("flag"))) > 0)

# calculate what percentage of entries differ by variable
diff_summary <- acs_2021_merged %>%
  summarise(across(ends_with("flag"), ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))

# calculate the number of entries by the size of differences in index_value
score_diff <- acs_2021_merged %>%
  mutate(index_diff = index_value_new - index_value_old) %>% 
  select(geoid, state_name_old, county_name_old, index_value_old, index_value_new, index_diff) %>% 
  filter(index_diff > 0) %>% 
  count(index_diff)
```

```{r}
## comparing 2023 acs df to original 2021acs df
# Compare missingness
missing_old <- data_catalog_index_old %>% 
  summarise(across(everything(), ~mean(is.na(.)))) %>% 
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "missing_rate_old")


missing_new <- data_catalog_2023_acs %>% 
  summarise(across(everything(), ~mean(is.na(.)))) %>% 
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "missing_rate_new")

missing_comparison_year <- full_join(missing_old, missing_new, by = "variable")

# 2. Compare distributions for numeric variables
numeric_vars <- data_catalog_index_old %>% select(where(is.numeric)) %>% names()

data_catalog_index_old %>%
  count(index_value, sort = TRUE)

# Plot histograms side-by-side
plot_list <- map(numeric_vars, function(var) {
  combined <- bind_rows(
    data_catalog_index_old %>% select(all_of(var)) %>% mutate(source = "data_catalog_index_old"),
    data_catalog_2023_acs %>% select(all_of(var)) %>% mutate(source = "data_catalog_2023_acs")
  )
  
  ggplot(combined, aes_string(x = var, fill = "source")) +
    geom_histogram(alpha = 0.6, position = "identity", bins = 100) +
    labs(title = paste("Distribution of", var), x = var, y = "Count") +
    facet_wrap(~ source)
})



# export results
write_csv(score_diff, "2021_acs_score_differences.csv")

write_csv(missing_comparison, "2021_acs_missing_comparison.csv")

write_csv(missing_comparison_year, "new_old_missing_comparison.csv")


pdf("plots_output.pdf", width = 8, height = 6)  # Set PDF output file and dimensions

for (plot in plot_list) {
  print(plot)  # Print each plot to the PDF
}

dev.off() 
```
